intro: GOOSE is how protection relays, the devices that open a breaker when a line has a fault, tell each other to trip in a few milliseconds. It runs over the substation network instead of copper wires. A relay publishes its data to a multicast address: one message that every device on the network hears. Every relay that needs the data subscribes to it. Nobody answers, so the publisher repeats each change, fast at first and then slower.
plain: When a power line fails, the safety devices in a substation must react within a few thousandths of a second. This message works like a fire alarm that every room hears: one device calls out the news once, to everyone, and the devices that care act on it. Nobody replies, so the sender repeats the call several times, quickly at first, to make sure it is heard.

heartbeat.title: All is well
heartbeat.text: Nothing is wrong. Every second, the relay repeats its last state to anyone listening. This heartbeat tells the subscribers that the relay and the network still work.

fault.title: A short circuit
fault.text: A short circuit on feeder F1, one of the lines leaving the substation. The relay measures 2.8 kA. It closes its trip contact, a wired signal that makes breaker Q1 open.

publish.title: Announce the trip
publish.text: At the same moment, the relay sends its new state to every subscriber. The state number (stNum) goes up by one. The sequence number (sqNum), which counts the copies of one state, starts again at 0.

repeat.title: Repeat fast
repeat.text: No subscriber answers GOOSE, so the relay sends the same message again 2 ms after the change, then at 4, 8 and 16 ms, and so on, until it is back to once a second.

act.title: Subscribers react
act.text: F2 PROT watches breaker Q1 in case Q1 fails. It starts a timer: if Q1 has not opened when the timer runs out, F2 PROT trips the other breakers that feed the fault. The gateway passes the trip on to SCADA, the control center's system.

open.title: Breaker opens
open.text: 48 ms after the trip, Q1 is open and the fault current stops.

frames.trip-wire: Energize the trip coil of Q1

notes.trip-wire: A copper wire, not a network message: the relay closes a contact and current flows into the breaker's trip coil.
notes.to-scada: This is IEC 104, not GOOSE: the gateway translates between the two. The IEC 104 lesson shows these bytes.
notes.opened: An auxiliary contact, a switch that moves with the breaker, tells the relay that the breaker has opened.

dst.name: Destination
dst.note: A multicast address from the range IEC 61850 keeps for GOOSE (01-0C-CD-01-…). Every device on the network hears it; only subscribers keep it.

vlan.name: VLAN tag
vlan.note: 0x8100, then priority 4 and VLAN 10. The priority lets switches send the frame ahead of other traffic.

ethertype.name: EtherType
ethertype.note: 0x88B8 means GOOSE. There is no IP and no TCP in this frame.

appid.name: APPID
appid.note: 0x0001: an ID for this stream of messages. Subscribers filter on it.

length.name: Length
length.note: 115 bytes, from the APPID to the end.

reserved.name: Reserved
reserved.note: Two reserved fields, zero here. IEC 62351-6 uses them when the frame is signed.

pdu.name: GOOSE message
pdu.note: 0x61 starts the message; 105 bytes follow (0x69). Each field after it is a tag, a length and a value.

gocbref.name: gocbRef
gocbref.note: Tag 0x80, 25 bytes: the name of the control block that sends this message, F1PROTLD0/LLN0$GO$gcbTrip.

tal.name: Time allowed to live
tal.note: 2000 ms. If no copy arrives within this time, subscribers treat the data as invalid.

datset.name: datSet
datset.note: The data set: the list of values this message carries, F1PROTLD0/LLN0$dsTrip.

goid.name: goID
goid.note: F1PROT_Trip: an ID that subscribers can check.

t-old.name: t
t-old.note: When the data last changed: 08:00:00 today, UTC. A heartbeat keeps the time of the last change.

t-event.name: t
t-event.note: When the data changed: 10:41:07.232 UTC. 4 bytes of seconds, 3 of fractions of a second, 1 of clock quality.

stnum-12.name: stNum 12
stnum-12.note: The state number: still 12, so the data has not changed.

stnum-13.name: stNum 13
stnum-13.note: The state number went up by one: the data changed.

sqnum-3.name: sqNum 3
sqnum-3.note: The sequence number counts the copies of one state, from 0: this is the fourth copy.

sqnum-0.name: sqNum 0
sqnum-0.note: The first copy of the new state.

simulation.name: simulation
simulation.note: False. True marks test messages, which subscribers ignore unless they are in test mode.

confrev.name: confRev 1
confrev.note: The configuration revision. It must match the one the subscriber was set up with.

ndscom.name: ndsCom
ndscom.note: Needs commissioning: false. True would mean the publisher's setup is incomplete.

data-idle.name: allData
data-idle.note: The values: Tr.general = FALSE (no trip), and its quality: good.

data-trip.name: allData
data-trip.note: The values: Tr.general = TRUE (trip!), and its quality: good.

a-ied.name: IED
a-ied.note: The device's name in the SCL file.

a-ld.name: Logical device
a-ld.note: LD0: a logical device, a group of functions inside the IED.

a-ln.name: Logical node
a-ln.note: LLN0: the logical node of the device itself, where the control blocks live.

a-fc.name: Functional constraint
a-fc.note: GO: what follows is a GOOSE control block.

a-cb.name: Control block
a-cb.note: gcbTrip: the name of the control block.

facts.between: One relay → every relay, controller and gateway that subscribes
facts.frames: One message, repeated: no requests, no answers
facts.speed: A trip must arrive within 3 ms (IEC 61850-5, type 1A)

tips: A subscriber checks the gocbRef, the APPID, the data set and the configuration revision. If one differs from its setup, it ignores the frame and says nothing.
GOOSE has no IP address, so routers drop it. To reach another substation you need R-GOOSE.
Test with the simulation flag and the subscriber in test mode. Otherwise a test trip opens a real breaker.
Every switch on the way must keep the VLAN tag and its priority. A switch that strips it can delay a trip behind other traffic.

timing.title: Why GOOSE never waits for an answer
timing.note: GOOSE has no acknowledgment. The publisher repeats each change quickly, then slows down to a heartbeat. If a subscriber hears nothing within the time allowed to live, it marks the data invalid. The repeat times here are typical; each vendor sets its own.
